## The wall batch: booking the wall changes of a stage at once (no switch) {#sec-ch10-wallbatch}

### Summary

Each prescribed-face apply (@sec-ch10-prescribed) books a weighted sum per row. Booking each apply separately would
cost a few launches every time; the wall batch instead collects every apply's changes of a stage, for the hydro
and scalar registers and all three directions, and books them together at the end of the stage. It keeps the
changes in fixed device storage, so that a captured stage books exactly what the eager stage books.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Collect each apply's change (after minus before) with its face-area weights, then book every slot's
weighted row sums at the stage's end ([-@eq-ch10-wallbatch-flush]).

**Data.** One fixed buffer per block, one slot per register and direction in the stage's push order, with the
face areas laid out the same way.

**Placement.** Started at the top of the stage's advance; flushed in the stage combine, before `end_stage`.

**Activation.** On for every block (the hydro and scalar registers share it); a register without a batch books at
the call.

**Guarantee / limits.** Graph equals eager bitwise: every slot is a plain weighted sum, no scatter-add.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of this section.
:::

Local symbols: $\boldsymbol\delta_k$ is slot $k$'s change, rows by faces; $\mathbf w_k$ its face-area weights.

### Derivation

A push copies $\boldsymbol\delta_k = \mathbf T^{\mathrm{after}} - \mathbf T^{\mathrm{before}}$ on the written faces into
slot $k$. The flush books, for each slot and row $r$,

$$
\mathbf M_{\mathrm{p}}[r] \mathrel{+}= \sum_{f} \mathbf w_k[r, f]\,\boldsymbol\delta_k[r, f],
$$ {#eq-ch10-wallbatch-flush}

The flush is {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp WallBatch::flush >}}.

which is ([-@eq-ch10-prescribed-book]) summed over the stage's applies. The order of the slots is the order of the
pushes, so a register and direction applied twice in a stage (the explicit total, then after the implicit
correction) books both applies.

### Numerical method

The batch registers a slot at its first push of a stage pattern (eager, before any capture); the slot remembers
the monitor and amount it books, the number of rows and faces, and the weight tensor it was registered with. A
later push to the same slot only copies into the buffer. A register that rebuilds its weights is a new slot. The
flush computes each slot's product with its weights, sums the rows, books one rate per row, then zeroes the
buffer. Fixed storage matters for capture: a host queue of the changes would be emptied by the first warm-up of a
captured combine and never refilled by a replayed advance, so the replayed stages would book nothing while the
state stayed equal. The buffer is registered with the block's state store, so a capture's warm-ups restore it.
The batch's place in the stage is shown in @fig-ch10-register-order.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| push a change | {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp WallBatch::push >}} | `push` | none |
| book and zero | {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp WallBatch::flush >}} | `flush` | none |
| drop a rejected attempt's changes | {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp WallBatch::clear >}} | `clear` | none |
| start the stage's slots | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_advance >}} | `stage_advance` | none |
| flush before `end_stage` | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_combine >}} | `stage_combine` | none |
| fixed storage | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::register_flux_storage >}} | `register_flux_storage` | none |

: The code of the wall batch. {#tbl-ch10-wallbatch-code}

Walk-through: `stage_advance` starts the batch at its first slot every pass and clears it at stage 0, so a
rejected attempt's changes are dropped; `overwrite_` pushes; `stage_combine` flushes, then calls `end_stage`.

### Limits

A slot pattern that changes inside a capture is not allowed: slots are registered eagerly, and a new pattern
rebuilds the buffer. Switch combinations are in @sec-ch12-matrix.
